title: Talk2Build. The meeting that ships.
s01_hook: Three friends, one deadline. The pizza is twenty-five minutes out, and they want a game before it lands. Talk2Build sits in the meeting, with Alexa plus as its voice.
s02_goal: Maya says the goal out loud. Nobody types a command. A plan card appears, and the decision and action items are saved under her name.
s03_design: Chris sketches the architecture. Priya asks for the game screen. Both land on the shared stage while they are still talking.
s04_evidence: Then the classic argument: Phaser or PixiJS? This card is live. Real GitHub and npm numbers, each with its source. Talk2Build recommends. The humans decide: plain canvas, zero dependencies.
s05_pizza: Is the pizza here yet? Small talk gets parked. It stays out of the plan.
s06_phone: A feasibility card for phones: plain canvas works, as long as it gets touch controls.
s07_yes: Chris asks for the build. Anything that writes code waits for a human yes. Maya says yes. Talk2Build writes a spec from the meeting's decisions, scaffolds the prototype from its game-jam template, and runs the tests. Seven of seven pass.
s08_play: And here it is, playable right inside the meeting. Space Cat Courier. Dodge the asteroids, grab pizza for fuel. Every ten parcels, the asteroids speed up.
s09_pizza: Then the real pizza arrived. Parked, naturally.
s10_end: End the meeting. The minutes, the spec, the designs and the prototype stay in the workspace.
s11_how: Under the hood, Alexa plus talks to a self-hosted MCP server over Streamable HTTP, and the tools do the work. This demo runs in mock mode, on recorded fixtures.
